The races identify the *net* cost of one step harder over a whole stint, holding stint length and race phase fixed: Budapest 2023 +0.022 +/- 0.181 s [not used: standard error 0.181 s > 0.15 s (pre-2026 measurement, too imprecise to pool)]; Budapest 2024 -0.114 +/- 0.437 s [not used: standard error 0.437 s > 0.15 s (pre-2026 measurement, too imprecise to pool)]; Budapest 2025 -0.029 +/- 0.307 s [not used: standard error 0.307 s > 0.15 s (pre-2026 measurement, too imprecise to pool)]; australia-2026 +0.317 +/- 0.345 s; japan-2026 -0.069 +/- 0.664 s; barcelona-2026 +0.060 +/- 0.336 s; austria-2026 +0.106 +/- 0.295 s; belgium-2026 +0.075 +/- 0.323 s; italy-2026 +0.173 +/- 0.354 s -> pooled +0.131 +/- 0.143 s per step. The model's fresh-tyre offsets are calibrated so that, with its own degradation ladder, it reproduces this net at the stint length it recommends.

regime.derivation: race/practice degradation ratio, stint-fixed-effects estimator on both sessions; residuals pooled with the median: australia-2026 0.75x, japan-2026 0.73x, barcelona-2026 0.70x, austria-2026 0.58x, belgium-2026 0.32x, italy-2026 0.81x -> management residual 0.72x (spread 0.28 ln); no temperature term (no race-day forecast supplied: no temperature term); the pool gives 0.72x; Budapest's own practice->race ratio in [2023, 2024, 2025] is 0.38x (+/-0.28 ln), which carries 49% of the precision, so 0.53x applies; the old pooled geometric mean would have given 0.62x. hungary-2026's own race is never used
